Audience: every first-time South Carolina Class D applicant; these habits apply from the first permit drive.
Why it matters to a first-timer: the minimum four-second following distance and how to count it are set out here [A06], along with the state law on signaling before a lane change, turn or merge [A09].
Level: a mix of exact values (look-ahead seconds, following seconds, perception and reaction times, braking distance, flood depths, signal distance) and judgment about space and speed.
Prerequisites: the lane change, passing and highway entry rules from the previous section, which this section builds on.
